content: 1. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 2. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of erythromycin base by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Both chlorpromazine and erythromycin base prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Erythromycin base and the cholera vaccine exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cholera vaccine should not be administered to patients who have received systemic antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 5. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, reduce the cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily. 6. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Ciprofloxacin and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin coadministration with QT-prolonging drugs may increase the risk of torsades de pointes, though the risk is lower compared to other quinolones. 9. Erythromycin base increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both citalopram and erythromycin base prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Clarithromycin increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and vice versa. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Clindamycin and erythromycin base exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially reducing each other's effects. The clinical significance is unknown. 12. Clindamycin topical and erythromycin base also exhibit pharmacodynamic antagonism, with unknown clinical significance. 13. Both clomipramine and erythromycin base prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base also increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Erythromycin base decreases the activation of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing clopidogrel's bioactivation. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Erythromycin base increases clozapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Cobicistat and erythromycin base increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir. 17. Erythromycin base increases cobimetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If short-term use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg daily. Resume the original dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor. 18. Erythromycin base increases colchicine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (P-gp). Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the colchicine dose as per prescribing guidelines. Colchicine use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 19. Erythromycin base increases conivaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and vice versa. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Erythromycin base increases conjugated estrogens' levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. It may also decrease their levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Erythromycin base increases cortisone levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Cortisone decreases erythromycin base levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Crizotinib increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Erythromycin base also increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Crofelemer increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Crofelemer minimally inhibits systemic CYP3A4 due to low absorption. 24. Cyclophosphamide increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 25. Erythromycin base increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Cyclosporine also increases erythromycin base levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Erythromycin base increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Avoid coadministration in patients with atrial fibrillation and CrCl <30 mL/min or DVT/PE treatment with CrCl <50 mL/min. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Dabrafenib decreases erythromycin base levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 28. Erythromycin base increases dactinomycin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Erythromycin base increases dalteparin effects by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Danazol increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 31. Danicopan increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider dose reduction of P-glycoprotein substrates when coadministered with danicopan. 32. Erythromycin base increases dapsone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Erythromycin base increases daridorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit daridorexant dose to 25 mg per night when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 34. Darifenacin increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and vice versa. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Erythromycin base increases darolutamide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4. Monitor closely for adverse reactions and adjust darolutamide dose as needed. 36. Erythromycin base increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and vice versa. This combination is contraindicated. 37. Dasatinib and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Dasatinib also increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and vice versa. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Erythromycin base increases daunorubicin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Deferasirox decreases erythromycin base levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Erythromycin base increases deflazacort levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose when coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 41. Both degarelix and erythromycin base prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Both desflurane and erythromycin base prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Both desipramine and erythromycin base prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Erythromycin base increases desloratadine levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 45. Deutetrabenazine and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death when using QT-prolonging drugs. 46. Erythromycin base increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Dexamethasone decreases erythromycin base levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. DHEA increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 48. Erythromycin base increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 49. Erythromycin base increases diazepam buccal and intranasal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce diazepam elimination, increasing adverse reactions. 50. Erythromycin base decreases dicloxacillin effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 51. Erythromycin base increases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism but may decrease their levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely.
